architecture_candidates.reason: At verified VCC=1.8 V the any-pin maximum is 2.2 V; an actual 3.3 V host drive exceeds it by 1.1 V. Absolute maximum is not an operating target. Host drive and physical DUT identity remain unverified.

architecture_candidates.oe: Design OE low as disabled intent. Bias, control voltage, power-off behavior and sequencing implementation unresolved.
architecture_candidates.reason: Three fixed A-to-B and one B-to-A channels match standard SPI directions. 3.3 V VCCA and 1.8 V VCCB targets are within documented supply ranges; this does not establish logic or timing margins.

source_refs.paraphrase: Standard SPI uses DI as the device input and DO as the device output, with CLK and chip select as device inputs.
source_refs.section: 4.2 Serial Data Input, Output and IOs

source_refs.paraphrase: The pin table defines three A-side inputs driving B-side outputs and one B-side input driving an A-side output.
Both supply rails have a recommended operating range beginning at 1.08 V and extending to 5.5 V.
Driving output enable low places all translator outputs in their high-impedance state.
TI shows an SPI mapping, while explicitly treating application information as outside the component specification and requiring design validation.

architecture_candidates.reason: Two shared-direction pairs yield 4+0, 2+2 or 0+4 channel capacities, not 3+1. Both target rails fit the documented supply range but cannot fix this topology mismatch. This conclusion is limited to one device for the stated mapping.

source_refs.paraphrase: The four channels are split into two two-bit sections, each controlled by one shared direction input.
Both supply rails have a recommended operating range of 0.65 V through 3.6 V.
Each section's direction input selects A-to-B or B-to-A for that entire two-channel section.
